chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I said to him, 'What is the least of what would suffice the sick, from the Glorification during the Rukūʿ and the Sajdah?' He said, 'One Glorification'.
ai.seo_question: What is the minimum amount of Tasbīḥ required for a sick person in prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the legal principle of *rukhsah* (concession) for the ill, establishing that a single recitation of the Tasbīḥ suffices in both Rukūʿ and Sajdah, contrasting with the standard practice of three. It reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on easing religious obligations (*taysīr*) for those with valid excuses, ensuring that the integrity of prayer is maintained without imposing undue hardship.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Yunus Bin Abdul Rahman, from Muawiya Bin Ammar, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘
I said to himasws, ‘What is the least of what would suffice the sick, from the Glorification during the Rukū and the Sajdah?’ Heasws said, ‘One Glorification’.
en.sarwar: 4. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Yunus ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman from Mu‘awiyah ibn ‘Ammar who has said the following: “I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, ’
How many Tasbih is sufficient in Ruku’ (bowing down on one’s knees) and in Sujud (prostration) in the case of one suffering from illness?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘One Tasbih is sufficient.’”
